answer: To resist sybil attacks in an agent economy, require each new agent to deposit a time-locked bond of resources that can only be unlocked after proving sustained useful work, such as completing verified logistics tasks. An attacker spinning up many fakes would face rising marginal costs as the knoll of required collateral grows with each duplicate identity, while genuine operators who ship real cargo from the lotus pier to the wharf recover their stake through settled fees. This ties identity cost directly to economic output rather than cheap account creation.
